name: SushiSwap RouteProcessor2 approval exploit (0xsifu) - rescue-turned-feeding-frenzy
era: post-merge, pre-mempool-dumpster (no mempool archive: in-block evidence only)
verdict_reason: Copy chain reconstructed on-chain. The first RP2 call that pulled 100 WETH from the victim's approval in public history is Yoink's tx in 17007838 (idx 23). (sent by the white-hat Trust, mined one block LATER at 17007839 idx 54) except the 20-byte fake-pool address. Trust's tx had maxFee 18.8724 gwei < block 17007838 base fee 18.8779 gwei so it could not be included in 17007838: Yoink pre-empted a still-pending tx. 10 further copiers/rescuers followed in 17007839-17007856, all with the same route diff (only bytes 249-268). c0ffeebabe's 17007842 idx 0 tx is the 9th of 11 pulling txs (8 pulls in one tx), not the first. Our call-level comparison for c0ffeebabe.eth transactions is withheld by policy; the public traces can be compared by anyone.
protocol_loss_usd: about 3.3M (reported: PeckShield/BlockSec); on-chain: 18 x 100 WETH = 1800 WETH pulled from one wallet in blocks 17007838-17007856
key_correction: The 'original attacker' is not a hacker: it is the white-hat Trust (@trust__90) doing a public-mempool rescue of the victim's approved WETH. DeFiHackLabs (Sushi_Router_exp.sol) lists c0ffeebabe's copy 0x04b166e7... as 'the TX'; BlockSec cites 0x43ff7e01... (Trust's) as the first attack tx; neither is the earliest on-chain pull (Yoink 0xb8f57cf8..., block 17007838).

payments_summary.claim_checked: BlockSec: ~44.5% of losses went to block builders. Reproduced from traces: 44.8% (806.98 of 1800 ETH)
payments_summary.nuance: Payments reach builders only in transit: in 17007839 the builder used the proposer's fee recipient (0x388c818c..., Lido-labelled vault - public knowledge, not re-verified here) as block.miner, so the 107.096 ETH of bot payments went straight to the validator; in 17007842 beaverbuild.org received 689.235 ETH gross and paid the proposer 689.017 ETH (margin 0.218 ETH = 0.03%); 17007840 rsync margin 0.0005 ETH; 17007856 Flashbots margin 0.0004 ETH. 'Went to builders' = went to the auction; ~99.9% ended with proposers.

auction.headline: Only the Flashbots relay still serves 2023 bids; the winning blocks were delivered via Agnostic (17007839, 17007842) and the Flashbots relay (17007856); 17007838 and 17007841 were not MEV-Boost blocks (no bids; vanilla geth extraData / empty extraData); 17007840's delivering relay is not among the answering relays (winner rsync-builder.xyz submitted an 11.047 ETH block to the Flashbots relay at +775 ms while other builders' bids on that relay reached 20.82 ETH).

headline_text: Yoink copied the white hat Trust's still-pending RouteProcessor2 rescue one block early (17007838 idx 23); the copy frenzy then sent 44.8% of the 1,800 WETH pulled to the block auction, and 875 ETH was later returned.

harmonized.verdict_reason: Yoink's pull in 17007838 pre-empted white hat Trust's still-pending rescue (max fee below that block's base fee); route bytes identical except the fake-pool address. There is no hostile attacker.
